"I want to underline that while we may have become free from the British constitutionally and geographically, nearly 80 years have passed, yet we have still not liberated ourselves from the English language. items.title: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam move Supreme Court seeking bail in Delhi riots conspiracy case
items.summary: Delhi riots conspiracy case accused Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved the Supreme Court seeking bail. They have challenged the September 30 order of the Delhi High Court denying them bail. The Delhi High Court had observed that the Supreme Court had earlier denied bail to Khalid and Imam in January 2026, stating that they can file for bail again after a year or after the protected witnesses have been examined. The High Court said that since the two conditions have not been met yet, granting bail to Khalid and Imam would amount to modifying the Supreme Court order, which the High Court cannot do. “In view of the above discussion and overall facts of these cases, specifically the conditions imposed by the Supreme Court in Gulfisha Fatima, this court cannot find fault with the order passed by the trial court. The present appeals are therefore dismissed,” the High Court said. This is the second time Khalid and Imam are approaching the Supreme Court seeking bail. The most recent order of the top court came in January 2026 when five people were granted bail, but Khalid and Imam were declined relief . They then once again moved the trial court which rejected their pleas on July 4 .

items.title: Fake histories, dubious authorship: Perumal Murugan questions Periyar Arivulagam book procurements (97)
items.summary: Controversy has erupted over book procurements at the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library and science centre in Coimbatore after writer Perumal Murugan allegedly uncovered exorbitantly priced books of questionable authorship filled with falsified information. One such book is on a made up chief minister. Another claims that the Naladiyar—an ancient collection of Tamil poems—was a person. A third seems to attribute short stories to modern Tamil poet and writer Bharathiyaar that he likely never wrote. Perumal also raised the question if these ‘books’ are simply AI-generated text from fake publishing houses that were set up expressly for supplying to the library. The allegations have triggered a political storm between the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and the opposition Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), with the government announcing an inquiry into the purchases. In an article titled Periyar Arivulagathil Periya Oozhal (Major Scam in Periyar Arivulagam), published on the Tamil portal Sindhai on November 6, Perumal said he found nearly 1,800 books published by a company called Agal Vilakku Pathipagam on the library's fourth floor.
